name: IN-02
label: Likely R

key_factors: Incumbent Yakym with large fundraising edge ($5.2M vs $356K)
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~4%
No polling or expert ratings available
model.rationale: Yakym holds a heavily Republican seat with a massive financial advantage, and markets give Decio only a ~4% chance. With no polls or ratings suggesting movement, the fundamentals point to a comfortable Republican win.
model.watch: A major late-breaking scandal or a sharp national Democratic wave could narrow the margin, though a seat flip remains unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northern Indiana's second district is solidly Republican territory, with a partisan lean of about thirteen points toward the GOP. Rudy Yakym, the incumbent, is running for reelection with a commanding financial advantage, having raised over five million dollars to challenger Jamee Decio's roughly three hundred fifty thousand. A Libertarian candidate also appears on the ballot.

No public polling or expert ratings exist for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, money, and prediction markets, all of which point strongly to Yakym. The forecast expects a Republican win by a wide, double-digit margin, with low but nonzero uncertainty given the absence of direct polling.
